newsitem.title: UK: Dollar/mark rebounds from lows, gains seen limited.
newsitem.headline: Dollar/mark rebounds from lows, gains seen limited.

text.p: The dollar rebounded from the one-week low it set against the mark Monday, though its gains were expected to be limited as long as talk of a delay to European economic and monetary union persists.

Concern EMU won't start on time was triggered Monday after France asked for time to consider a pact which requires countries to maintain fiscal discipline after they join EMU. This boosted the mark against other European and the dollar.
While short covering lifted the dollar from its lows against the mark Tuesday, it will struggle to extend its gains until an accord on the stability pact is reached, analysts said.

"The fundamentals are very supportive of the dollar, and the market is short after the move yesterday," said Lee Ferridge, the currency strategist at Commerzbank. "But given all the doubts about EMU, I don't expect the move to go too far or last too long."
The dollar was steady against the yen, meantime after U.S. officials repeated their support for a strong U.S. currency and a Japanese officials spoke out against excessive currency moves.
Dollar/mark was quoted at 1.7130/35 at 0805 GMT from its 1.7020 low Monday and 1.7055/60 late yesterday in Europe. Dollar/yen was at 112.90/3/30 from 112.65/75 Monday.

French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn and other European Union officials yesterday said the delay to approving the stability pact was not a precursor to renegotiating it and reiterated their commitment to launching EMU on time in 1999.

Still, traders will remain jittery about the outlook for EMU until France gives its verdict on the stability pact. French European Affairs Minister Pierre Moscovici said Tuesday Paris needs more than a week to study the pact and carry out an audit of state finances.
Traders are now looking to the meeting between Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok and French President Jacques Chirac today.

Elsewhere, the dollar was supported against the yen after Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said currency moves have been excessive and that Japan will combat excessive swings in an appropriate and timely way.

Speaking a day after the dollar tumbled more than two yen to a six-month low of 111.80, Mitsuzuka also said Japan will discuss exchange rates and its trade surplus with other members of the Group of Seven leading industrial nations at their June 20-22 meeting in Denver.
The dollar was also supported after American officials called for a strong dollar Monday.

Traders are also looking for direction to the Japanese April current account data to be published at 2350 GMT Tuesday. Economists polled by Reuters are expecting a rise in the surplus to 1.1 trillion yen from 1.0 trillion in March.

"A rebound will reinforce worries about the underlying uptrend in the Japanese trade figures and could see the yen test its highs," said Nick Stamencovic, an economist at DKB International. "But if it does, you can expect to see the Japanese authorities trying to talk the yen down again." -Swaha Pattanaik, London Forex Desk +44 171 542 6284
